messages:
alex.support: Heads-up — ACME reported repeated failures when using streaming + function-calling. They see incomplete JSON for tool args and our SDK fails with \"Unexpected end of JSON input\". Customer repros with cURL and small keepalive chunks. They attached a snippet, asking for root cause and workaround.

jess.engineer: Can you paste the exact raw response bytes they captured? Is this via SSE or raw chunked HTTP (Transfer-Encoding: chunked)? Also need request-id from the failing call.

alex.support: They said Transfer-Encoding: chunked, using our JS SDK with streaming enabled and function calls. Request-id: req_6b2f1c. Raw captured fragment (customer trimmed stacktrace):
```
data: {"id":"resp_01","event":"tool_call","payload":{"name":"charge_customer","arguments":{"invoice_id":"inv_12345","amount": 4999
```
The stream ends there (client receives EOF) -> parser throws. They claim full-arg payload exists on server side for non-streaming calls.

rafael.eng-runtime: Hmm. That pattern looks like the trailing bytes got cut off mid-number/field. Two hypotheses: (1) upstream edge/proxy is splitting a multi-byte UTF-8/JSON token into separate TCP frames without proper chunk coalescing leading to client-side parse if reader treats each chunk as a separate event; (2) our streaming layer emitted SSE frames mid-object then closed stream prematurely. Any chance the SDK is re-parsing per-chunk instead of buffering until a full JSON object is delimited?

jess.engineer: SDK v2 does incremental JSON assembly but relies on complete SSE event boundaries (\n\n) — if the middleware converts arbitrary TCP chunks into SSE events incorrectly it will cause this. Can support reproduce against staging by hitting the same route with keepalive/slow-client flags?

alex.support: ACME provided a minimal repro curl command:
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"xlarge","stream":true,"functions":[{"name":"charge_customer","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"invoice_id":{"type":"string"},"amount":{"type":"integer"}}}}],"input":"charge for inv_12345"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate --no-buffer
```
They then simulate a slow network and show the response bytes in sequence: 
1) `data: {"id":"resp_01","event":"tool_call","payload":{"name":"charge_customer","arguments":{"invoice_id":"inv_12345","amount": `
2) `data: 4`
3) `data: 999`
4) `data: }}}\n`
Customer parser expects a single continuous JSON object inside the payload; seeing the `4` and `999` arrive as separate SSE data events breaks their JSON assembly logic.

rafael.eng-runtime: Thanks — that clarifies it's SSE event fragmentation. We saw a similar symptom once when our router (midplane) forwarded application-level SSE frames without reassembling underlying chunk boundaries. Router was flushing on 128B writes. I need logs for req_6b2f1c from the router and the serving host.

maya.platform: cc-ing eng-platform for visibility. @rafael.eng-runtime do we have telemetry on event emission sizes around that time window? If router is flushing small writes, we might need a quick config change to coalesce writes for SSE or add a reassembly buffer server-side before emitting SSE data.

rafael.eng-runtime: Quick mitigation we can ask ACME to try: a) disable streaming (non-ideal), b) upgrade to SDK that buffers SSE data across events until a full JSON parse is possible, or c) set X-Redwood-Stream-Mode: framed which will send complete JSON objects per event (we have a non-default option). I'll check if framed mode is available on hosted API for them.

jess.engineer: Could also add a short-lived workaround in the router: enable small coalescing window (50ms) on streaming routes for customers on older SDKs. That should reduce mid-object splits. Will need a controlled rollout.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: midplane-write-coalesce toggle -> staging at 2023-11-02T03:00:00Z, canary at 2023-11-02T04:00:00Z.

rafael.eng-runtime: I pulled logs for req_6b2f1c — see entries: "emit chunk size=96 flush=true" repeatedly while sending a 512-byte payload. Router flushed multiple 96B frames then closed stream after final write. This matches customer traces. Root cause: midplane configured with aggressive buffering/flush on close.

maya.platform: Proposed fix: change midplane buffer policy to coalesce writes until either newline or max-coalesce-size 1024 bytes, and update streaming contracts to prefer framed SSE when function-calling. I'll open a small PR to change default to coalesce=512 and expose runtime flag per-tenant.

alex.support: I'll share mitigation steps with ACME: toggle framed mode or disable streaming for the route until we flip the coalesce flag. They prefer not to disable streaming. Can we enable framed for just their tenant?

rafael.eng-runtime: Yes — we can flip framed mode on tenant acme-prod via feature-flag for now. I'll apply to staging and run the repro.

alex.support: ACME confirmed they repro locally with curl. They asked us to test on staging with their token. I'll follow up with them once we have a flag change. :thumbsup:

jess.engineer: After flag flip, we should also add a regression test: slow-client SSE assembly that verifies events containing JSON payloads are valid when reassembled. Will add to runtime test-suite.

maya.platform: Created ticket INF-8721 for midplane coalesce change + per-tenant framed fallback. Assigning to rafael.

rafael.eng-runtime: On it. I'll post follow-up with staging request-id and deploy notes once ready.

alex.support: Thanks team — escalating to ACME is paused until we validate on staging. Will update when customer confirms.
_meta: generated: support thread about streaming tool-call arg truncation — contains reproduction, logs, and proposed mitigation steps
